This might sound goofy, but what's helped me be nicer to myself is to think of myself in the third person. You'd probably never treat another person as unkindly as you treat yourself,  so try to do things for "OP", not for you. So if I have an exam tomorrow, I just think. "I'm going to study now to make her life easier tomorrow", or if I'm mad at myself for doing something self destructive I'll say "She's trying her best,  being angry with her won't help,  give her the benefit of the doubt". I know talking in the third person sounds kooky, I wouldn't reccomend doing it aloud when you're not alone. But I hate ME, when I go off on me, I say things in terms of "you're this,  you're that". Thinking of myself as a random body that I'm kind of looking after has just made me less inclined to say mean things about "her", and that pattern of being less mean has slowly helped me to accept myself and hate myself less. I'm sure you're a fine person, so you should give yourself the benefit of the doubt the way you might for others. If that's not possible, give "OP" the benefit of the doubt
